answer.generated: In object database systems, object-identifiers share similarities with pointers in pointer-based models in terms of their underlying functionality of uniquely identifying objects. However, unlike pointers which are typically not visible at the logical level, object-identifiers operate at a higher level of abstraction where their existence is acknowledged, thus providing a more structured approach to object identification within these advanced database systems. This difference in visibility highlights the evolution towards more sophisticated and abstract data management techniques in modern database systems, distinguishing them from earlier pointer-based models.
